```{r}
#| label: setup

L  = bridge$likelihood

TR = oc$trajectory
RP = oc$replays

P  = lfd$profiles

step_col = c(M0 = "grey20", M1 = "#7D3C98", M1b = "#B07CC6", M2 = "#2471A3", M3 = "#C0392B")
model_col = c("MFCL M3" = "grey20", O0 = "#7D3C98", O1 = "#2471A3", `O1-mid` = "#C0392B")
sb_at = function(s, y) TS[step == s & year == y, sb]
dep_at = function(s, y) TS[step == s & year == y, depletion]
o1_lb = oc$o1$par[["log_B0"]]
o1m_lb = oc$o1_mid$par[["log_B0"]]
```

# Overview

This document converts the 2024 stock assessment of south Pacific albacore
(*Thunnus alalunga*) [@teears2024alb], a two-region MULTIFAN-CL [MFCL,
@fournier1998mfcl; @davies2025mfcl] model, into opal, an RTMB
age-structured model with one region. Any model runs here are preliminary
explorations and should not be used *as is* for management advice. opal is
not changed: where it cannot represent the MFCL model, the MFCL model is
simplified (in MFCL) or the difference is measured with replays (standalone
simulations) and documented. The comparisons are meant as advice to opal's
developers on the features the stock would need.

* **An MFCL bridge to model region 1** (@sec-bridge). Five steps, each a
  refitted MFCL model: the diagnostic model (M0), no movement (M1), the
  movement weeks moved onto fishing dates (M1b), region 1 only (M2), and
  growth fixed without the conditional age-at-length data (M3). Region 1's spawning biomass roughly doubles at each step: the
  stock's scale is weakly determined, and each source of information removed
  lets it drift up.
* **The conversion** (@sec-convert) maps MFCL's October-September model
  year, its quarterly and monthly fishing incidents, the indices and the
  length compositions onto opal with four seasons, and takes biology at age
  from MFCL.
* **At MFCL's values opal reproduces MFCL** (@sec-o0): its initial numbers
  and recruitment exactly, its spawning biomass within
  `r pct(max(abs(TR[model == "O0", sb] / TR[model == "MFCL M3", sb] - 1)))`.
  Replays put the gap on catch timing (start-of-quarter removal against
  MFCL's Baranov removal at each incident's date); seasonal selectivity
  hardly matters for spawning biomass.
* **The fits** (@sec-fits). With MFCL's selectivity fixed, opal's scale is
  unbounded (O1): the length compositions keep improving towards an
  unexploited stock. The cause (@sec-lf) is length-at-age timing: MFCL
  predicts each length sample at its date with lengths that grow through
  the year, opal from start-of-year length-at-age. With opal's growth at
  MFCL's mid-year lengths (O1-mid) the fit is bounded, with B0 at MFCL's
  Beverton-Holt B0; opal's stock is still about half MFCL's in 2022,
  because MFCL starts far above its own unfished equilibrium (@sec-start).
  Estimating the initial population (O1i) brings it close to MFCL's. With
  opal's own selectivity (@sec-o2) the double normals collapse to
  knife-edges and the stock is a quarter of MFCL's.
* **Seasonal set-ups** (@sec-seasonal). Splitting the fisheries with
  seasonal selectivity into one fishery per season, and an opal model with
  quarterly age classes and time steps (recruitment kept annual), are set up
  through opal's inputs alone.
* **What opal would need** is summarised in @sec-gaps.

# The 2024 assessment {#sec-assessment}

The assessment [@teears2024alb] covers the south Pacific from the equator to
50°S and from 140°E to the coast of South America, in two regions: region 1
is the southern WCPFC Convention Area, including the overlap area with the
EPO, and region 2 the rest of the EPO. Fisheries are defined as areas-as-fleets
within each region (six areas in region 1, three in region 2).

* **Time.** 1954 to the third quarter of 2022. The model year runs
  October-September with recruitment on 1 October (week 37 of the calendar
  year in the report), 12 annual age classes (the last a plus group); catches
  are taken by quarter (longline, driftnet) or month (troll).
* **Fisheries.** 17 extraction fisheries (13 in region 1: longline by flag
  group and area, two troll fisheries and a driftnet fishery; 4 in region 2)
  and three index fisheries (region 1: longline north of 25°S and New
  Zealand troll; region 2: longline). Catches are in numbers except troll and
  driftnet (weight). The catch-conditioned approach solves the Baranov catch
  equation for fishing mortality at each fishing incident.
* **Indices.** sdmTMB standardised CPUE [@anderson2022sdmtmb] with
  time-varying CVs; the troll index's generic CV is set to 0.2.
* **Length compositions.** 50 2-cm bins from 30 cm, re-weighted by catch;
  robust normal likelihood; sample sizes capped at 1000 and divided by
  Francis [-@francis2011] weights; samples below 50 fish dropped.
* **Conditional age-at-length.** 654 otolith ages in 33 fishery-quarter
  strata, effective sample size 0.75 of the observed.
* **Biology.** von Bertalanffy growth with offsets at ages 2-4 (L~1~ fixed
  at 45.5 cm); M-at-age inversely proportional to length [@lorenzen1996],
  scaled to average 0.36 over ages 4-12; spawning potential from maturity
  and sex ratio at length; Beverton-Holt steepness 0.8 with a weak penalty
  (CV 0.71) on recruitment deviations; fixed recruitment distribution (0.819
  in region 1) and movement from SEAPODYM [@senina2020seapodym].
* **Selectivity.** Length-based cubic splines (3-4 nodes), grouped across
  fisheries (16 groups), seasonal (four seasons) for the tropical longline
  fisheries 1-7 and the EPO fishery 14, non-decreasing for the longline
  indices.

The assessment found the stock not overfished and not subject to
overfishing (median SB~recent~/SB~F=0~ 0.48 across the model ensemble,
including estimation uncertainty).

# The MFCL bridge {#sec-bridge}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-bridge
#| tbl-cap: "The MFCL bridge (M0 diagnostic, M1 no movement, M1b movement weeks on fishing dates, M2 region 1 only, M3 growth fixed without age-at-length). Objective (negative log-likelihood plus penalties) and its components; region 1 spawning (adult) biomass in thousand tonnes; depletion in 2022 against the unfished projection (none for M1b, whose zero-fishing projection MFCL stops). M0-M1b's region 1 values are from two-region models."
B = merge(L, TS[year == min(year), .(step, sb_1954 = sb / 1000)], by = "step")
B = merge(B, TS[year == max(year), .(step, sb_2022 = sb / 1000, depletion)], by = "step")
knitr::kable(B[, .(step, objective = fmt(objective, 1),
                   length = fmt(length_comp, 1), `age-length` = fmt(age_length, 1),
                   CPUE = fmt(cpue, 1), `max grad.` = sci(max_gradient),
                   `SB 1954` = fmt(sb_1954, 0), `SB 2022` = fmt(sb_2022, 0),
                   depletion = fmt(depletion, 3))], format = "pipe")
```

The diagnostic model was supplied with MFCL 2.2.7.0, which reproduces its
objective function value exactly (M0). Each later step is refitted with the
diagnostic model's phase 9 settings (2200 evaluations), warm-started from
the previous step; a fit takes 15-20 minutes. M1 and M3 stop at the
evaluation limit with the line search stalled, at maximum gradients of a few
times 10^-6^.

* **M1, no movement.** The (fixed, SEAPODYM-derived) movement matrices are
  set to the identity, so the regions are closed populations. They still
  share the recruitment deviations (total recruitment split 0.819 / 0.181)
  and the stock-recruitment relationship, so the EPO data still inform
  region 1's recruitment.
* **M1b, movement weeks on fishing dates.** The movement weeks change from
  37, 5, 17 and 29 (1 October and the first weeks of February, May and
  August) to 5, 17, 29 and 41 (February, May, August and November), all
  region 1 fishing dates. With no movement this changes nothing but MFCL's
  time steps: it removes the extra period at the start of each year that
  MFCL adds at a movement week in a multi-region model, which a one-region
  model does not have (see the transplant check below), so that M1b-M2
  changes only the regions. MFCL's zero-fishing projection for M1b stops
  with a "sanity error" (the first period of a year is no longer a movement
  period), so M1b has no depletion; its fit converges.
* **M2, region 1 only.** The EPO fisheries (14-17) and EPO index (20) are
  dropped and the region 1 indices renumbered 14 and 15. The par file is
  built from M1b's: fishery- and region-indexed values are subset, region 1's
  recruitment is kept by shifting the total population scaling parameter by
  log(0.818971), and the sections shaped by regions, movement or catch
  records come from MFCL's `-makepar` for the one-region files (all zero or
  structural in this model). M2 removes the recruitment link to the EPO.
* **M3, growth fixed, no age-at-length.** opal has no conditional
  age-at-length likelihood, so growth is fixed at M2's estimates and the
  data dropped.

```{r}
#| label: fig-bridge
#| fig-cap: "Region 1 spawning biomass and depletion along the MFCL bridge."
p1 = ggplot(TS, aes(year, sb / 1e3, colour = step)) + geom_line() +
    scale_colour_manual(values = step_col) + labs(x = NULL, y = "SB (kt)", colour = NULL)
p2 = ggplot(TS, aes(year, depletion, colour = step)) + geom_line() +
    scale_colour_manual(values = step_col) + labs(x = NULL, y = "SB / SB(F=0)", colour = NULL) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1))
p1 + p2 + plot_layout(guides = "collect")
```

Region 1's spawning biomass in 1954 goes from `r fmt(sb_at("M0", 1954) / 1e3, 0)`
kt (M0) to `r fmt(sb_at("M1", 1954) / 1e3, 0)`, `r fmt(sb_at("M2", 1954) / 1e3, 0)`
and `r fmt(sb_at("M3", 1954) / 1e3, 0)` kt, and depletion in 2022 from
`r fmt(dep_at("M0", 2022), 2)` to `r fmt(dep_at("M3", 2022), 2)`. In this
catch-conditioned model the scale comes from the indices, the length
compositions and their interaction with the catch; movement, the shared
recruitment with the EPO and the age-at-length data each constrain it, and
it drifts up as each is removed.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-transplant
#| tbl-cap: "Transplant checks: M2's one-region structure evaluated (no refit) at M1's and at M1b's estimates against their region 1. Largest relative difference."
knitr::kable(bridge$transplant_check[, .(quantity, `vs M1` = sci(vs_m1, 1), `vs M1b` = sci(vs_m1b, 1))], format = "pipe")
```

With no movement, region 1 in M1 is unaffected by region 2's catch or
abundance (tested by setting region 2's catch and recruitment near zero),
and M2's inputs match its region 1 exactly: every `.frq` record (catch,
effort, CV and length frequencies) and every flag and parameter section of
the par file, with the total population scaling parameter shifted by exactly
log(0.818971). Recruitment, selectivity, growth, M and the predicted catches
agree, but against M1 the numbers at the oldest ages drift up by a few
percent and adult biomass by up to
`r pct(bridge$transplant_check[quantity == "adult biomass", vs_m1])`.

The cause is in how MFCL builds its time steps. Each region's year is split
into periods at its fishing incidents and, in a multi-region model only, at
the movement dates (`check_for_missing_node()` in `rnaux2.cpp` returns the
movement nodes only `if (num_regions > 1)`). Natural mortality is shared
equally among a year's periods (`fraction = -log(n)`), not by elapsed time,
and acts together with F in each period. MFCL's year has 48 weeks (four per
month); the movement weeks are calendar weeks, renumbered into the
October-September model year like the records (`get_history_data()`,
"renumber for month_1"). The diagnostic model's weeks 37, 5, 17 and 29 are
1 October (the start of the model year) and the first weeks of February, May
and August. Region 1 fishes in February, May and August but never in
October, so M1's region 1 has an extra period at the start of every year,
which M2 (one region) does not. Moving the movement weeks onto fishing
dates (M1b) removes the extra periods and the difference falls from
`r pct(bridge$transplant_check[quantity == "numbers at age (all years)", vs_m1])` to
`r pct(bridge$transplant_check[quantity == "numbers at age (all years)", vs_m1b], 2)` in
numbers-at-age and from
`r pct(bridge$transplant_check[quantity == "adult biomass", vs_m1])` to
`r pct(bridge$transplant_check[quantity == "adult biomass", vs_m1b], 2)` in adult
biomass. What is left is confined to the initial age structure (0.02% per
age in 1954, gone by 1990), which MFCL builds from the average Z of the
first ten periods, whose layout at the start of the series still differs.
Removing regions therefore changes MFCL's within-year timing of M as well
as the data and the recruitment link; M1b separates that structural effect
(M1-M1b) from the change of regions (M1b-M2).

# Conversion to opal {#sec-convert}

`shared/mfcl-to-opal/` reads MFCL's `.par`, `.frq`, plot report and
`length.fit` in base R and builds opal's inputs (`mfcl_to_opal()`).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fisheries
#| tbl-cap: "Fisheries in opal (M3). MFCL diagnostic: the fishery number in the two-region model. Seasons: distinct selectivity patterns by season in MFCL. Length data: the fish flag 49 divisor of the capped sample sizes, the number of quarters and of model years with compositions."
F = oc$fisheries
knitr::kable(F[, .(fishery, `MFCL diagnostic` = mfcl_diagnostic, name, `catch units` = units,
                   `catch total` = fmt(catch_total, 0), seasons = sel_seasons,
                   divisor = lf_divisor, quarters = lf_quarters, years = lf_years)], format = "pipe")
```

* **Time.** MFCL's model year starts in calendar month 10: the `.frq`
  dimension line's ninth field (MFCL's `month_1`), which the report gives as
  week 37. Calendar months 10-12 belong to the next model year (so the
  data's last model year, 2022, has no calendar October-December). opal has
  69 model years of four seasons (October-December, January-March, ...),
  with recruitment and ageing at the start of the year. Fishing incidents in
  the same fishery and season are summed (troll catches are monthly).
* **Catch** is in numbers for the longline fisheries and in tonnes for troll
  and driftnet; the two indices remove nothing.
* **Indices.** MFCL's survey likelihood is log-normal with variance
  $\lambda_i \sigma^2$, where $\lambda_i$ is the `.frq` CV column over its
  mean and $\sigma$ fish flag 92 / 100 (0.2): opal's standard errors are
  $\sigma \sqrt{\lambda_i}$. Both indices are annual (longline in July-September,
  troll in January-March).
* **Length compositions.** Samples below 50 fish are dropped, each is
  rescaled to its sample size capped at 1000, and they are summed by
  fishery and model year, with MFCL's divisors as opal's variance
  adjustments, under opal's multinomial likelihood (MFCL: robust normal per
  incident).
* **Biology.** Mean weight, maturity and M at age from MFCL's report, so
  opal's spawning biomass is MFCL's adult biomass (numbers x weight x
  maturity at the start of the year). opal's growth is used only for the
  length compositions: von Bertalanffy with age-specific K multipliers at
  ages 1-4 for MFCL's independent mean lengths at ages 2-4 (RMSE
  `r fmt(sqrt(mean((oc$growth$opal_length - oc$growth$mfcl_length)^2)), 2)` cm),
  SD linear in mean length between MFCL's SDs at ages 1 and 12 (largest
  difference `r fmt(max(abs(oc$growth$opal_sd - oc$growth$mfcl_sd)), 2)` cm).
* **Selectivity.** MFCL's selectivity-at-age, averaged over seasons
  weighted by each season's catch (index fisheries: their survey season),
  as opal's `sel_fa_external`.

# opal at MFCL's values {#sec-o0}

O0 holds everything at MFCL M3's values. `mfcl_match_recruitment()` sets
opal's B0 from MFCL's Beverton-Holt curve ($R_0 = \alpha - \beta / \text{SPR}_0$,
$B_0 = R_0 \text{SPR}_0$), its initial deviations so that opal starts from
MFCL's 1954 numbers-at-age, and its recruitment deviations (bias adjustment
off) so that it recruits MFCL's recruitment every year.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-o0
#| tbl-cap: "O0 against MFCL M3: largest relative differences."
knitr::kable(oc$o0_check[, .(quantity, `max rel. diff.` = sci(max_rel_diff, 1))], format = "pipe")
```

The replays are standalone simulations with MFCL's estimates (not opal
code). They cross catch removal at the start of each quarter, then a quarter
of M (opal), or MFCL's catch-conditioned Baranov in each fishing period
(the year's distinct incident dates, each with an equal share of the year's
M, as MFCL apportions it), with MFCL's season-averaged selectivity (opal) or
its seasonal selectivity.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-replays
#| tbl-cap: "Replays: spawning biomass against MFCL M3 (relative difference in 2022 and largest annual) and against O0."
knitr::kable(RP[, .(`rel. 2022` = pct(rel_mfcl[.N], 2), `max |rel.|` = pct(max(abs(rel_mfcl)), 2),
                    `max |rel.| vs O0` = pct(max(abs(sb / opal_o0 - 1)), 2)),
                by = .(timing, selectivity)], format = "pipe")
```

The opal-timing replay with averaged selectivity reproduces O0, which
checks the replay. Catch timing accounts for almost all of the gap between
O0 and MFCL; seasonal selectivity changes spawning biomass by less than 0.1%.
The MFCL replay is within 0.5% of MFCL (0.6% with M shared by elapsed time
instead); the remainder is largest in the mid-1990s, after the driftnet
years, and may be the weight-at-age MFCL uses for catches in weight (not
confirmed).

```{r}
#| label: fig-o0
#| fig-cap: "Spawning biomass relative to MFCL M3: O0 and the replays."
ggplot(RP, aes(year, rel_mfcl, colour = paste(timing, selectivity, sep = " / "))) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") + geom_line() +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(100 * x, "%")) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "SB relative to MFCL", colour = "timing / selectivity")
```

# opal fits {#sec-fits}

O1 holds MFCL's season-averaged selectivity, growth, steepness (0.8),
sigma~R~ (`r fmt(oc$o1$sigma_r, 2)`, MFCL's CV of 0.71), M and the biology,
and estimates B0, the recruitment deviations for 1955-2020 (the last two at
the curve, as MFCL sets them at the mean), and the two index catchabilities.
The initial population is unfished. O1 runs to the upper bound of log(B0)
(`r fmt(o1_lb, 2)` against MFCL's `r fmt(lb_mfcl, 2)`): spawning biomass in
the billions of tonnes and depletion near 1.

```{r}
#| label: fig-profile
#| fig-cap: "Profile over log(B0) for O1 (recruitment deviations and catchabilities estimated at each value): change in the objective and its components from their smallest values. The dashed line is MFCL's scale."
pr = melt(PR[, .(log_B0, total = objective, cpue, `length comps` = lf, recruitment = rec)],
          id.vars = "log_B0")
pr[, delta := value - min(value), by = variable]
ggplot(pr, aes(log_B0, delta, colour = variable)) + geom_line() + geom_point() +
    geom_vline(xintercept = lb_mfcl, linetype = 2) +
    labs(x = "log(B0)", y = "change in negative log-likelihood", colour = NULL)
```

Here and below, "MFCL's scale" is MFCL's Beverton-Holt B0 (log(B0)
`r fmt(lb_mfcl, 2)`), the value O0 uses. The index and the recruitment
penalty are best near it; the length
compositions keep improving towards an unexploited stock and win.

# Why the length compositions favour an unexploited stock {#sec-lf}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-lf-fishery
#| tbl-cap: "Length-composition negative log-likelihood by fishery in the O1 profile, at MFCL's scale and at log(B0) 3 higher (start-of-year growth)."
bf = lfd$by_fishery[variant == "annual"][order(change)]
knitr::kable(bf[, .(fishery, name, `n obs` = n_obs, `at MFCL` = fmt(at_mfcl, 1),
                    `at +3` = fmt(at_plus3, 1), change = fmt(change, 1))], format = "pipe")
```

The longline fisheries drive the pull; the troll fishery 11 prefers MFCL's
scale. With selectivity fixed, a lightly fished stock keeps more large, old
fish, so opal's predicted longline catches are too small for the data.

MFCL predicts each length sample at its date. Its `length.fit` gives, for
each sample, the predicted composition by age, whose mean lengths show
length-at-age growing through the model year (@fig-laa); opal predicts every
sample from start-of-year length-at-age.

```{r}
#| label: fig-laa
#| fig-cap: "MFCL's mean length-at-age by model month (month 1 is October), from its predicted length compositions by age (M3), with opal's start-of-year length-at-age (points at month 1)."
lm_dt = data.table(month = rep(1:12, ncol(lfd$laa_month)), age = rep(seq_len(ncol(lfd$laa_month)), each = 12),
                   length = as.vector(lfd$laa_month))
ggplot(lm_dt[age <= 8], aes(month, length, colour = factor(age))) + geom_line() +
    geom_point(data = data.table(month = 1, age = 1:8, length = oc$growth$opal_length[1:8])) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12) +
    labs(x = "model month", y = "mean length (cm)", colour = "age")
```

The test changes only opal's inputs: its growth fitted to MFCL's mid-year
lengths (the average of model months 6 and 7). @fig-lf-profiles compares
profiles over B0 for the annual model with start-of-year and mid-year growth,
the same with fisheries 1-7 split into one fishery per season
(@sec-seasonal), and the quarterly-age model.

```{r}
#| label: fig-lf-profiles
#| fig-cap: "Profiles over log(B0) (relative to MFCL's): change in the total objective (left) and in the length-composition component (right). annual: O1's set-up; -mid: growth at MFCL's mid-year lengths; split: one fishery per season for fisheries 1-7; quarterly: quarterly ages (B0 on the annual model's scale)."
pp = P[is.finite(objective)]
g1 = ggplot(pp, aes(dlog_B0, d_objective, colour = variant)) + geom_line() + geom_point() +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2) + labs(x = "log(B0) - MFCL's", y = "change in objective", colour = NULL)
g2 = ggplot(pp, aes(dlog_B0, d_lf, colour = variant)) + geom_line() + geom_point() +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2) + labs(x = "log(B0) - MFCL's", y = "change in length comps", colour = NULL)
g1 + g2 + plot_layout(guides = "collect")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-lf-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Profile summaries: where the objective is smallest (log(B0) relative to MFCL's), how much it rises at +5, and depletion at MFCL's scale."
knitr::kable(lfd$summary[, .(variant, `best log(B0) - MFCL's` = fmt(best_dlog_B0, 2),
                             `rise at +5` = fmt(rise_at_plus5, 1),
                             `depletion at MFCL's scale` = fmt(depletion_at_mfcl_scale, 3))], format = "pipe")
```

With mid-year growth the profile has a minimum near MFCL's scale and the
index fit improves, and O1-mid (O1 with mid-year growth, B0 estimated)
converges at log(B0) `r fmt(o1m_lb, 2)` against MFCL's `r fmt(lb_mfcl, 2)`.
The length compositions on their own still favour a somewhat larger stock
than MFCL's.

## Starting population {#sec-start}

A B0 at MFCL's does not give MFCL's stock. MFCL scales its initial
population with its own parameter (the total population scaling), separately
from its stock-recruitment relationship, and its 1954 spawning biomass
(`r fmt(TR[model == "MFCL M3" & year == min(year), sb] / 1e3, 0)` kt) is about
`r fmt(TR[model == "MFCL M3" & year == min(year), sb] / exp(lb_mfcl), 0)` times its
Beverton-Holt B0, with 1954 recruitment
`r fmt(TR[model == "MFCL M3" & year == min(year), recruits] / mean(TR[model == "MFCL M3", recruits][-1]), 1)`
times its mean. O0 reproduces it only by imposing MFCL's initial numbers
(`init_rdev_a`); fitted opal models start from the unfished equilibrium at
B0, as the assessment report describes but MFCL does not implement. O1-mid's
spawning biomass is
`r fmt(TR[model == "O1-mid" & year == min(year), sb] / 1e3, 0)` kt in 1954 and
`r fmt(TR[model == "O1-mid" & year == max(year), sb] / 1e3, 0)` kt in 2022,
against MFCL's `r fmt(TR[model == "MFCL M3" & year == max(year), sb] / 1e3, 0)` kt.
Estimating the initial population, as MFCL does, closes most of the gap
(O1i, @sec-o2).

The quarterly-age model, which gives each quarter MFCL's length-at-age and
selectivity and fits the length compositions by quarter, also has its
minimum at MFCL's scale and fits the indices far better than any annual
variant (CPUE negative log-likelihood
`r fmt(P[variant == "quarterly" & abs(dlog_B0) < 1e-8, cpue], 2)` at MFCL's
scale, against `r fmt(P[variant == "annual-mid" & abs(dlog_B0) < 1e-8, cpue], 2)`
for annual-mid and `r fmt(P[variant == "annual" & abs(dlog_B0) < 1e-8, cpue], 2)`
for the O1 set-up). Its depletion at that B0
(`r fmt(P[variant == "quarterly" & abs(dlog_B0) < 1e-8, depletion_end], 3)`) is
lower than the annual variants', partly because its stock-recruitment curve
is evaluated differently (@sec-seasonal); its B0 is not comparable with the
annual models' beyond being a scale.

```{r}
#| label: fig-fits
#| fig-cap: "Spawning biomass and dynamic depletion: MFCL M3, O0, O1 and O1-mid. O1's spawning biomass is off the scale."
g1 = ggplot(TR[model != "O1"], aes(year, sb / 1e3, colour = model)) + geom_line() +
    scale_colour_manual(values = model_col) + labs(x = NULL, y = "SB (kt)", colour = NULL)
g2 = ggplot(TR, aes(year, dynamic_depletion, colour = model)) + geom_line() +
    scale_colour_manual(values = model_col) + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1.05)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "SB / SB(F=0)", colour = NULL)
g1 + g2 + plot_layout(guides = "collect")
```

# Seasonal set-ups {#sec-seasonal}

Both set-ups use opal's inputs only.

**Seasonal fisheries** (`mfcl_split_seasonal_fisheries()`). Fisheries 1-7,
whose MFCL selectivity differs by season, become four fisheries each (36
fisheries), each with one season's catch, selectivity and length
compositions. This represents MFCL's seasonal selectivity exactly in the
annual-age model and lets opal estimate seasonal curves; on its own it does
not change the length-composition pull (@fig-lf-profiles).

**Quarterly ages** (`mfcl_quarterly_ages()`). opal's time step and age
classes become quarters: 48 quarterly ages and 276 steps, one season each.
Recruitment stays annual: the recruitment deviations of the three quarters
without recruitment are fixed at -30, and the initial numbers of quarterly
ages that do not exist (cohorts recruit once a year) are near zero. Then:

* quarterly age $q = 4(a - 1) + s$ holds annual age class $a$ in season
  $s$ only, so a selectivity by quarterly age is MFCL's seasonal selectivity
  (exactly, except for the plus group, which is present in every season);
* length-at-age, and weight at the time of catch, are MFCL's at each
  quarter's fishing month (opal's growth fitted to them, RMSE
  `r fmt(sqrt(mean((lfd$quarterly_growth$opal_length - lfd$quarterly_growth$mfcl_length)^2)), 2)` cm);
* the length compositions are fitted by quarter, and the indices in the
  quarter they sample;
* M is MFCL's per quarter.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-o0q
#| tbl-cap: "Quarterly-age model at MFCL's values against MFCL M3."
knitr::kable(lfd$o0q_check[, .(quantity, `rel. diff.` = sci(rel_diff, 1))], format = "pipe")
```

The cost is the stock-recruitment relationship: opal treats every step as a
recruitment, so with one recruitment in four steps its B0 is about four times
the unfished spawning biomass and the curve is evaluated at a quarter of the
usual relative stock size, which changes what steepness means. Depletion has
to be taken against opal's unfished projection, and B0 treated as a scale
parameter.

# Fits with the quarterly ages and opal's own selectivity {#sec-o2}

Five further fits (`scripts/05-fit-opal-selectivity.r`), with growth,
steepness, sigma~R~, M and the biology held as in O1. All estimate the
initial population (@sec-start): one deviation for the 1954 recruits (age 1)
and one shared by the older ages, which sets the level of the initial age
structure (in the quarterly models the plus group has its own), without the
penalty against the stock-recruitment relationship (opal's
`lambdas$init_rec = 0`), as in MFCL.

* **O1i**: O1-mid (annual, mid-year growth, MFCL's selectivity) with the
  initial population estimated.
* **O1q**: the quarterly-age model with MFCL's seasonal selectivity fixed;
  B0, the first-quarter recruitment deviations (1955-2020), the initial
  population and the catchabilities estimated.
* **O2**: the annual model with mid-year growth (O1-mid) and opal's own
  length-based selectivity: double normals (a logistic for the longline
  index, which MFCL holds non-decreasing), shared within MFCL's selectivity
  groups (fisheries 1 and 3, 2 and 4, 5 and 6). Three of the double
  normal's six parameters are estimated: the peak and the two widths, within
  bounds (peak within 2 SD of the length bins, widths in [-6, 3]). The
  plateau and final selectivity are held at the starting curves', which are
  fitted to MFCL's selectivity-at-age through opal's length-at-age, and the
  initial selectivity near zero. (A first attempt with five of the six free
  ran most widths, plateaus and final selectivities to their bounds.)
* **O2-split**: O2 with fisheries 1-7 split into one fishery per season,
  sharing parameters within MFCL's groups and seasons.
* **O2q**: O1q with opal's own selectivity (one curve per group, whose
  selectivity-at-age varies by quarter through growth).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-o2
#| tbl-cap: "Fits with quarterly ages or opal's selectivity. Objectives of the quarterly models include a constant from the recruitment deviations fixed at -30 and are not comparable with the annual models'. At bound: estimated parameters at a bound. SB in thousand tonnes; depletion against opal's unfished projection."
SS = sel$summary
knitr::kable(SS[, .(model, `n par` = n_par, `max grad.` = sci(max_gradient), `at bound` = at_bound,
                    CPUE = fmt(cpue, 1), `length comps` = fmt(lf, 1),
                    `SB 2022` = fmt(sb_end / 1e3, 0), depletion = fmt(depletion_end, 3))], format = "pipe")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-o2
#| fig-cap: "Spawning biomass: MFCL M3 and the opal fits with MFCL's selectivity (O1-mid with the initial population at equilibrium; O1i and O1q with it estimated) or opal's own (O2, O2q)."
tr2 = rbind(TR[model %in% c("MFCL M3", "O1-mid"), .(model, year, sb)],
            sel$trajectory[model %in% c("O1i", "O1q", "O2", "O2q"), .(model, year, sb)])
ggplot(tr2, aes(year, sb / 1e3, colour = model)) + geom_line() +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "SB (kt)", colour = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-o2-sel
#| fig-cap: "Selectivity-at-age: MFCL's (averaged over seasons) and O2's estimates, for selected fisheries."
ff = c(3, 4, 6, 8, 11, 14)
sel_dt = rbind(
  data.table(source = "MFCL", fishery = rep(ff, each = 12), age = rep(1:12, length(ff)),
             sel = as.vector(t(oc$selectivity$average[ff, ]))),
  data.table(source = "O2", fishery = rep(ff, each = 12), age = rep(1:12, length(ff)),
             sel = as.vector(t(sel$fits$O2$sel_fya[ff, ]))))
sel_dt[, name := oc$fishery_names[fishery]]
ggplot(sel_dt, aes(age, sel, colour = source)) + geom_line() + geom_point(size = 0.8) +
    facet_wrap(~name) + labs(x = "age", y = "selectivity", colour = NULL)
```

With MFCL's selectivity, estimating the initial population brings opal close
to MFCL. O1i converges (largest gradient `r sci(SS[model == "O1i", max_gradient])`)
with `r fmt(SS[model == "O1i", sb_end] / 1e3, 0)` kt in 2022 and depletion
`r fmt(SS[model == "O1i", depletion_end], 2)`, against MFCL's
`r fmt(TR[model == "MFCL M3" & year == max(year), sb] / 1e3, 0)` kt and
`r fmt(TR[model == "MFCL M3" & year == max(year), dynamic_depletion], 2)`. O1q
(quarterly ages) agrees with it: the age-1 and older-age initial deviations
are close to O1i's and it ends at `r fmt(SS[model == "O1q", sb_end] / 1e3, 0)` kt.
In the quarterly models the plus group shares the older ages' initial level,
with its equilibrium offset supplied through `init_bias_adj_a` (a fixed
input; opal's map cannot tie parameters with an offset); estimated on its
own, it took the whole initial stock while the classes between went empty.

With opal's selectivity the fits do not settle on sensible curves, even with
three of the six parameters free. In O2 and O2q many double-normal widths go
to their bounds (knife-edge limbs), the largest gradients stay above 1, and
the stock is a quarter of MFCL's in 2022. O2-split ends at a point where the
gradient explodes as its curves collapse.

## Why the double normals collapse {#sec-collapse}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-collapse
#| tbl-cap: "O2 (opal's selectivity) against O1i (MFCL's), by fishery: length-composition negative log-likelihood, and the standard deviation of the observed and predicted compositions pooled over years (cm)."
sdv = function(p, L) { m = sum(p * L) / sum(p); sqrt(sum(p * (L - m)^2) / sum(p)) }
spread = sdg$pooled[, .(obs_sd = sdv(observed, length), O1i_sd = sdv(O1i, length), O2_sd = sdv(O2, length)), by = fishery]
bf = merge(sdg$by_fishery, spread, by = "fishery")[order(-gain)]
knitr::kable(bf[, .(name, `n obs` = n_obs, `O1i NLL` = fmt(O1i_nll, 1), `O2 NLL` = fmt(O2_nll, 1),
                    `observed SD` = fmt(obs_sd, 1), `O1i SD` = fmt(O1i_sd, 1), `O2 SD` = fmt(O2_sd, 1))],
             format = "pipe")
```

O2 gains most on the troll fisheries 11 and 12 and the longline fishery 3, and
loses on fishery 6. The northern longline fisheries' (3, 4, 6, 7) and the
longline index's compositions are narrower (SD 5.8-7.4 cm) than the model
predicts even with MFCL's selectivity, and about as narrow as the spread of
length within a single age at the ages they catch (MFCL's SD of length is
5.9-7.6 cm at ages 5-12). Under the multinomial likelihood every tail bin
counts, so opal narrows its predicted catch with a window-shaped selectivity
in length: the knife-edge widths, which flatten selectivity-at-age over the
older ages (@fig-o2-sel). MFCL's robust normal likelihood is much less
sensitive to the tails.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-lftests
#| tbl-cap: "Tests on O2 (and O1i) of the length-composition treatment (`scripts/07-test-lf-likelihood.r`): pool: tail bins below 0.5% and above 99.5% of each fishery's observed composition pooled; DM: Dirichlet-multinomial with each fishery's dispersion estimated; SD2: the SD of length at the oldest age estimated; all: the three together. Widths at bound: double-normal widths at a bound (of 22). Length-composition likelihoods differ in form between variants. SB in thousand tonnes."
LT = lft$summary
knitr::kable(LT[, .(model, `max grad.` = sci(max_gradient), `widths at bound` = widths_at_bound,
                    CPUE = fmt(cpue, 1), `length comps` = fmt(lf, 1), `SD oldest age` = fmt(sd2, 2),
                    `SB 1954` = fmt(sb_1954 / 1e3, 0), `SB 2022` = fmt(sb_2022 / 1e3, 0),
                    depletion = fmt(depletion_2022, 3))], format = "pipe")
```

Pooling the tails changes little. The Dirichlet-multinomial's dispersion
goes to its upper bound (the multinomial) for most fisheries, since the
sample sizes already carry MFCL's Francis weights, except the longline index
and the troll fisheries; the knife-edges remain. Estimating the SD of length
at the oldest age matters: the compositions want
`r fmt(min(LT[model %in% c("O2-SD2", "O2-all"), sd2]), 1)`-`r fmt(max(LT[model %in% c("O2-SD2", "O2-all"), sd2]), 1)` cm
instead of MFCL's `r fmt(LT[model == "O2", sd2], 1)`, fewer widths reach their
bounds, the index fit improves, and the scale changes from a quarter of
MFCL's to more than it. With all three (O2-all) the fit to both data types is
the best and the stock is closest to MFCL's
(`r fmt(LT[model == "O2-all", sb_2022] / 1e3, 0)` kt and
`r fmt(LT[model == "O2-all", depletion_2022], 2)` in 2022). The scale is
therefore sensitive to the assumed spread of length at age, which MFCL fixes
from its growth estimates with the age-at-length data. None of these fits is
fully converged (largest gradients 0.25-1.4) and 10-19 widths still sit at
bounds, so the selectivity remains to be constrained further (a width fixed,
priors, or age-based curves) with the SD of length estimated.

## Age-based and hybrid selectivity {#sec-agesel}

`scripts/08-fit-age-selectivity.r` evaluates the double normals on age
(opal's `sel_basis_f = 2`) instead of on length through the length-at-age
key, with the same three parameters free and the same groups; starting
curves are fitted directly to MFCL's selectivity-at-age. Growth then affects
only the predicted length compositions.

* **O3**: age-based curves for every fishery (the longline index logistic).
* **O3-SD2**, **O3-all**: as O2-SD2 and O2-all.
* **O4**: hybrid, with age-based curves for the longline fisheries and the
  index and length-based ones for the troll and driftnet fisheries (11, 12,
  13, 15).
* **O4-all**: O4 with tail pooling, the Dirichlet-multinomial and the SD of
  length at the oldest age estimated.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-agesel
#| tbl-cap: "Fits with age-based or hybrid selectivity, against O1i (MFCL's selectivity), O2 and O2-all (length-based). Widths at bound: double-normal widths at a bound (of 22). Length-composition likelihoods of the -all variants (pooled, Dirichlet-multinomial) differ in form from the others. SB in thousand tonnes."
AS = asel$summary
knitr::kable(AS[, .(model, `max grad.` = sci(max_gradient), `widths at bound` = widths_at_bound,
                    CPUE = fmt(cpue, 1), `length comps` = fmt(lf, 1), `SD oldest age` = fmt(sd2, 2),
                    `SB 1954` = fmt(sb_1954 / 1e3, 0), `SB 2022` = fmt(sb_2022 / 1e3, 0),
                    depletion = fmt(depletion_2022, 3))], format = "pipe")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-agesel
#| fig-cap: "Selectivity-at-age: MFCL's (averaged over seasons), O3's (age-based) and O4's (hybrid) for selected fisheries."
sa = asel$sel_age[model %in% c("MFCL", "O3", "O4") & fishery %in% c(3, 4, 6, 8, 11, 14)]
ggplot(sa, aes(age, sel, colour = model)) + geom_line() + geom_point(size = 0.8) +
    facet_wrap(~name) + labs(x = "age", y = "selectivity", colour = NULL)
```

Age-based curves keep MFCL's domed shapes, with far fewer widths at their
bounds, and fit every longline fishery's compositions better than MFCL's own
selectivity does (O1i). They fail for the troll fisheries: these catch young
fish (ages 1-4) whose lengths change quickly through the year, and a curve
on whole ages cannot follow which lengths are caught in each season, so O3
loses about 1000 units on fishery 11 alone. The hybrid O4 keeps the
age-based curves for the longline fisheries and length-based ones for troll
and driftnet. It fits the compositions better than any other multinomial
fit (O1i included), and its stock is the closest to MFCL's:
`r fmt(AS[model == "O4", sb_2022] / 1e3, 0)` kt and depletion
`r fmt(AS[model == "O4", depletion_2022], 2)` in 2022, against
`r fmt(TR[model == "MFCL M3" & year == max(year), sb] / 1e3, 0)` kt and
`r fmt(TR[model == "MFCL M3" & year == max(year), dynamic_depletion], 2)`. It is
not fully converged (largest gradient `r fmt(AS[model == "O4", max_gradient], 1)`)
and 7 widths are at bounds; with the SD of length estimated as well (O4-all)
the gradient is smaller but the stock lower
(`r fmt(AS[model == "O4-all", sb_2022] / 1e3, 0)` kt).

### Converging the hybrid, and its quarterly version

`scripts/09-fit-hybrid-selectivity.r` fixes each selectivity parameter that
O4 left at a bound at that bound and refits the rest (O4-fix), and fits the
hybrid on the quarterly-age model (O4q: age-based curves over the 48
quarterly ages for the longline fisheries and index, length-based for troll
and driftnet, the initial population estimated with the plus group tied,
started from O1q), then fixes its bounded parameters too (O4q-fix).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-hybrid
#| tbl-cap: "The hybrid selectivity model converged (O4-fix) and on quarterly ages (O4q, O4q-fix), with O1i and O1q (MFCL's selectivity) and O4. Fixed: selectivity parameters fixed at the bound O4 or O4q left them at. Quarterly models' objectives and length-composition likelihoods (by quarter) are not comparable with the annual models'. SB in thousand tonnes."
HY = hyb$summary
knitr::kable(HY[, .(model, `n par` = n_par, `max grad.` = sci(max_gradient), fixed = sel_fixed,
                    CPUE = fmt(cpue, 1), `length comps` = fmt(lf, 1),
                    `SB 1954` = fmt(sb_1954 / 1e3, 0), `SB 2022` = fmt(sb_2022 / 1e3, 0),
                    depletion = fmt(depletion_2022, 3))], format = "pipe")
```

Fixing the bounded parameters leaves the objectives unchanged and the fits
converge: O4's and O4q's large gradients were only those of parameters
pressing on their bounds. O4-fix (largest gradient
`r sci(HY[model == "O4-fix", max_gradient])`) keeps O4's result, the closest to
MFCL of the fits here. The quarterly hybrid O4q-fix also converges and fits
both the indices and the quarterly compositions better than O1q, but its
stock is about half O1q's (`r fmt(HY[model == "O4q-fix", sb_2022] / 1e3, 0)` kt and
depletion `r fmt(HY[model == "O4q-fix", depletion_2022], 2)` in 2022): on
quarterly ages the age-based curves are smooth in age across the seasons, so
they cannot follow MFCL's seasonal selectivity the way a quarterly-age
selectivity fixed at MFCL's values (O1q) does, and the scale moves with them.

# What opal would need {#sec-gaps}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-gaps
#| tbl-cap: "Features of the MFCL model that opal does not have, how they were handled here, and their effect."
gaps = data.table(
  MFCL = c("Two regions with movement; recruitment distributed over regions",
           "Conditional age-at-length likelihood",
           "Length compositions predicted at each sample's date, with within-year growth",
           "Seasonal selectivity (fisheries 1-7)",
           "Catch-conditioned Baranov at each fishing incident's date (several per quarter for troll)",
           "Length-based cubic-spline selectivity, grouped across fisheries",
           "VB growth with independent mean lengths at ages 2-4; SD log-linear in length",
           "Length compositions per incident, robust normal likelihood",
           "Index abundance at the incident's date",
           "Recruitment from the previous year's spawning potential; last two at the mean",
           "Initial population scaled by its own parameter, apart from the stock-recruitment relationship"),
  opal = c("one region",
           "none",
           "start-of-year length-at-age; annual compositions",
           "selectivity by year",
           "Pope removal at the start of each season",
           "logistic, double normal, double Richards; no mirrors (sharing via map)",
           "VB, Richards, cessation, age-specific K; SD or CV linear in length",
           "annual compositions; multinomial, Dirichlet, Dirichlet-multinomial",
           "start of the season",
           "same year's spawning biomass; free deviations",
           "unfished (or init_F) equilibrium at B0, with optional initial deviations"),
  here = c("MFCL bridge to region 1 (M1, M2); scale doubles at each step",
           "dropped with growth fixed (M3); scale doubles",
           "the main cause of O1's unbounded scale; mid-year growth or quarterly ages fix it",
           "catch-weighted average; <0.1% on SB; seasonal fisheries or quarterly ages represent it",
           "up to ~2% on SB (O0 against the replays)",
           "MFCL's selectivity-at-age fixed (O0, O1)",
           "age-specific K at ages 1-4 (0.5 cm RMSE)",
           "summed by fishery and year; Francis divisors kept",
           "as opal (season-start numbers)",
           "MFCL's recruitment imposed (O0); last two deviations fixed (O1)",
           "MFCL's initial numbers imposed in O0; fits start lower (MFCL's 1954 SB is ~5x its B0)"))
knitr::kable(gaps, col.names = c("MFCL", "opal", "here"), format = "pipe")
```

In order of their effect on this stock: length-at-age at the time of
sampling (or a sub-annual time step with annual recruitment, which would
also give seasonal selectivity, catch weight and index timing), then catch
timing within the season, then multiple regions, then a conditional
age-at-length likelihood for estimating growth.

# Reproducing this document

From any working directory (`CLAUDE.md` has the R environment):

```bash
Rscript --no-init-file case-studies/swpo-alb/scripts/01-build-mfcl-bridge.r
Rscript --no-init-file case-studies/swpo-alb/scripts/02-compare-mfcl-bridge.r
Rscript --no-init-file case-studies/swpo-alb/scripts/03-convert-fit-swpo-alb-opal.r
Rscript --no-init-file case-studies/swpo-alb/scripts/04-length-comp-diagnostics.r
quarto render case-studies/swpo-alb/vignettes/swpo-alb-mfcl-to-opal.qmd
```

The MFCL fits, opal fits and profiles are cached (`SWPO_ALB_REFIT=true`
repeats them). The document reads only `vignettes/data/`.
